newsitem.title: USA: Record China deficit keeps U.S. August trade gap up.
newsitem.headline: Record China deficit keeps U.S. August trade gap up.

text.p: The trade deficit narrowed in August, the Commerce Department said Friday, though a record deficit with China limited the monthly improvement.

The total trade deficit on goods and services fell 6.6 percent to $10.83 billion in August from $11.6 billion in July, coming in well above Wall Street economists' expectations for an $8.5 billion shortfall.
The gap with China shot up 23.4 percent to $4.71 billion in August, only the second time that China has surpassed Japan as the country with the biggest trade surplus with the United States.

By contrast, the deficit with Japan fell in August by 11.8 percent to $3.8 billion. The department said that during the first eight months of 1996, the cumulative deficit with Japan has fallen to $30.36 billion from $42.46 billion in the comparable 1995 period, the lowest since 1992.

But the deficit with China swelled to $24.25 billion in the first eight months this year from $21.8 billion last year as it continued to emerge as a key source of trade tensions for the United States.
The department said imports of Chinese-made items like toys and Christmas decorations jumped $301.8 million in August while clothing imports were up $86.9 million from July.
The United States typically runs a deficit on its trade with goods with the rest of the world that is partly offset by a surplus in services like tourism and insurance.
In August, the goods deficit widened by 2.9 percent to $16.99 billion while the services surplus rose 4.4 percent to $6.15 billion.
Total exports in August rose 3 percent to $69.32 billion after dropping 3.5 percent in July, while imports gained 1.6 percent to $80.15 billion after rising 1.3 percent in July.
